card.name: Punctuation and links inside medical lists
card.fires_on: Commas, periods, and small linking words like "of" or "have" that come right after a medical noun in drug-label or health text, where a list or next clause is expected.

modes.label: Punctuation after a condition
modes.description: A comma or period directly after a condition or problem noun, before the next item in a list or the next sentence.
modes.example: pulmonary disease or cor pulmonale, and those with a substantially decreased respiratory reserve, hypoxia<<,>> hypercapnia, or pre-existing respiratory

modes.label: Linking word after a noun
modes.description: The word "of" or "have" right after a noun such as overgrowth, family, or studies.
modes.example: prolonged use of cefepime for injection may result in overgrowth<< of>> nonsusceptible microorganisms.

modes.label: Inside a medical term
modes.description: The last piece of a long medical term, or the word intolerance.
modes.example: rare hereditary problems of galactose<< intolerance>>, severe lactase deficiency, or glucose

card.plain: It fires on the small commas, periods and linking words that follow a medical noun and lead into the next item or clause.
